title: Clinical Chemistry Analyzer

references.label: Standard clinical chemistry laboratory textbooks/manuals (e.g. Tietz Fundamentals of Clinical Chemistry)

purpose: Automates high-volume photometric (and often ion-selective electrode) testing of serum/plasma for the broad panel of routine clinical chemistry analytes — glucose, electrolytes, renal and liver panels, lipids, and more.
operatingPrinciple: Combines automated pipetting of sample and reagent, precisely timed incubation, and photometric (and/or ion-selective electrode, for electrolytes) measurement across many assay channels, applying the same absorbance-to-concentration principle the laboratory's spectrophotometer/Beer-Lambert entries already describe, scaled to run large test menus with minimal manual intervention.
basicOperation: Run calibration and QC material per the manufacturer's and laboratory's schedule before releasing patient results for each analyte.
Monitor reagent levels, onboard reagent stability/expiration, and sample/reagent probe function.
Review instrument flags for insufficient sample, clot detection, or reaction abnormality before accepting a result.
importantSettings: QC target ranges and acceptance rules
calibration: Calibrated per assay using manufacturer-traceable calibrators, verified against daily QC material and periodic proficiency testing.
maintenance: Routine probe/cuvette cleaning per manufacturer schedule to prevent carryover between samples.
Replace reagent packs and consumables before expiration.

commonErrors.cause: Hemolysis, lipemia, or icterus in the specimen interfering with the assay's photometric reading (see the related HIL concept)
commonErrors.fix: Check the specimen's H/I/L index against the assay's documented interference threshold before releasing the result

commonErrors.problem: QC out of range for one analyte channel
commonErrors.cause: Reagent lot change, calibration drift, or a probe/optics issue specific to that channel
commonErrors.fix: Recalibrate/troubleshoot per the laboratory's QC procedure before releasing further patient results on that channel

safety: Handle all serum/plasma samples and analyzer waste as biohazardous.
Follow manufacturer procedures for reagent handling, some of which contain hazardous chemicals.
